title: Discrete Isoperimetric Inequality (1D)
description: Formalization of the discrete isoperimetric inequality for finite subsets of Z. Proves that the edge boundary of any finite subset with at least 2 elements has size at least 2, with equality precisely for integer intervals.

meta.author: Classical
meta.assumptions: 0 axioms, 0 sorries. All results fully verified.
originalContributions: Edge boundary definition for finite subsets of Z
Lower bound: |dS| >= 2 for |S| >= 2 via min/max argument
Discrete isoperimetric theorem: intervals minimize boundary

overview.historicalContext: The discrete isoperimetric inequality is the combinatorial analogue of the classical isoperimetric theorem. In one dimension, the question is trivial: among all n-element subsets of Z, intervals have the smallest edge boundary (size 2). In higher dimensions, the problem becomes deep: Harper's theorem (1966) characterizes optimal sets in the hypercube, and the Loomis-Whitney inequality gives general bounds in Z^d.
overview.problemStatement: For a finite non-empty subset S of Z, prove that the edge boundary (adjacent integers not in S) has size at least 2. Prove that integer intervals achieve this bound exactly.
overview.text: The discrete isoperimetric inequality for Z: intervals minimize the edge boundary among all subsets of a given size.
overview.proofStrategy: The lower bound uses a simple min/max argument: the predecessor of min(S) and successor of max(S) are two distinct boundary points. For the equality case, we explicitly compute the boundary of [a,b] as {a-1, b+1}.
keyInsights: The min/max argument gives a clean, constructive proof of the lower bound
For intervals, the boundary consists of exactly two points at the endpoints
The 1D case is the foundation for higher-dimensional discrete isoperimetric inequalities

sections.title: Edge Boundary Definition
sections.summary: Defines the edge boundary of a finite subset S of Z and the IsInterval predicate.

sections.title: Boundary Lower Bound
sections.summary: Proves |dS| >= 2 for |S| >= 2 by showing the predecessor of min(S) and successor of max(S) are distinct boundary points.

sections.title: Interval Boundary
sections.summary: Proves that the edge boundary of [a,b] is exactly {a-1, b+1} with size 2.

sections.title: Discrete Isoperimetric Inequality
sections.summary: Combines the lower bound and interval equality into the discrete isoperimetric theorem for Z.

conclusion.summary: Fully verified (0 axioms, 0 sorries) formalization of the discrete isoperimetric inequality in one dimension. All results are constructive and do not depend on any axioms.
conclusion.implications: The 1D discrete isoperimetric inequality is the foundation for higher-dimensional results (Harper's theorem, compression arguments). The formalization demonstrates that the discrete analogue of the classical isoperimetric theorem has a clean, elementary proof.
openQuestions: Extend to Z^d using the Loomis-Whitney inequality or compression technique
Formalize Harper's theorem for the hypercube {0,1}^n
